basic_information.official_title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A BANGSAMORO MEMORIAL MARKER AND ECO-PARK IN CAMP ABUBAKAR, MUNICIPALITY OF BARIRA, MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE TO HONOR THE SHUHADA/MARTYRS OF THE BANGSAMORO STRUGGLE WHO GAVE AND DEVOTED THEIR LIVES FOR THE RIGHT TO SELF-DETERMINATION AND FREEDOM OF THE BANGSAMORO, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates a memorial marker bearing the names of the shuhada — those who gave their lives for Bangsamoro self-determination — set inside a public eco-park at Camp Abubakar in Barira, Maguindanao del Norte.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: To honour the martyrs of the struggle, and to do so in a place that is also usable: a landscaped park with a hall, a playground and facilities, reflecting Bangsamoro culture and arts.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: A memorial marker listing names is built within a new eco-park. A management board sets the criteria for whose names appear, determines the land, runs a grievance mechanism, and must consult local communities so the site has their ownership.
who_will_be_affected: Families of the shuhada, whose names may appear on the marker
Residents of Barira and visitors to the park
Indigenous peoples, whose distinct identity the policy section protects
Every province of the region, each of which has a seat on the board
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2024 — 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. A memorial listing the names of the shuhada will stand inside a public eco-park at Camp Abubakar — with a board that decides whose names appear, and a grievance mechanism if you disagree.
in_practice: The Bangsamoro Memorial Marker will carry a list of names of the shuhada
'Shuhada' covers those who gave and devoted their lives directly or indirectly in the armed struggle for Bangsamoro self-determination and freedom
The marker sits within a Bangsamoro Eco-Park at Camp Abubakar, Barira, Maguindanao del Norte

The park is to be landscaped and designed with structures and ornaments reflective of Bangsamoro culture and arts, with a multi-purpose hall, children's playground, parking, comfort rooms and wash areas, and access roads
A Bangsamoro Memorial Management Board chaired by the cultural heritage commission builds and runs it, with a representative from every province of the region
The Board sets the eligibility criteria for names, and must run a grievance mechanism
₱15,000,000 initial funding, with grants and donations — domestic or foreign — permitted
The Board dissolves once the project is completed and turned over to the cultural heritage commission

for_specific_groups.Families of the shuhada: Whether a name appears is decided against eligibility criteria the Board must establish, and there is a grievance mechanism if you dispute the outcome.
for_specific_groups.Residents of Barira: The local government has a seat on the Board, and the Board must consult and actively involve local communities to ensure their ownership of the site.
for_specific_groups.Indigenous peoples: The policy section states that indigenous peoples shall have the freedom to retain their distinct indigenous and ethnic identity in addition to their Bangsamoro political identity.
for_specific_groups.Every province: Each province of the BARMM has a representative on the Board.
for_specific_groups.Families and visitors: This is a park as well as a memorial — a hall, a playground and facilities, not only a monument.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: Camp Abubakar, Municipality of Barira, Maguindanao del Norte.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2024; construction depends on funding and the Board's work.
what_you_can_do: Ask the Bangsamoro Memorial Management Board for the eligibility criteria for inclusion of names
Use the grievance mechanism the Board is required to establish if a name is disputed
Take part in the community consultations the Board must conduct
watch_out_for: The eligibility criteria for names are not in the act — the Board sets them, and the final list goes to the Office of the Chief Minister.
The land area is not fixed by the act; the Board determines the metes and bounds.
₱15 million is an initial amount for a park with a hall, playground, roads and facilities.

key_terms_explained.Shuhada: Martyrs — here defined as those who gave and devoted their lives, directly or indirectly, in the armed struggle for Bangsamoro self-determination and freedom.
key_terms_explained.Camp Abubakar: The site in Barira, Maguindanao del Norte where the memorial and eco-park are to be built.
key_terms_explained.BMMB: Bangsamoro Memorial Management Board, which builds and manages the site until turnover.
key_terms_explained.BCPCH: Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage, which chairs the Board and takes over on completion.
key_terms_explained.Grievance mechanism: A route for disputes, which the Board must establish and keep functional.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Safar 15, 1446 / 19 August 2024, approved by the Chief Minister on 19 September 2024.

for_citizens: None. The act imposes no duty on the public.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences — it does not legislate on damage to or desecration of the memorial.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: The grievance mechanism the Bangsamoro Memorial Management Board is required to establish under Section 8(d)
where_to_complain.oversight: Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage, which chairs the Board and takes over on completion
where_to_complain.note: This is one of the few acts in the registry that expressly requires a grievance mechanism.

everyday_scenarios: A family believes their relative should be named on the marker. The Board must establish eligibility criteria, submits the final list to the Office of the Chief Minister, and must keep a grievance mechanism functional.
A family in Barira visits the site on a weekend. It is designed as an eco-park — hall, playground, parking, comfort rooms — not only as a monument.

A community group wants a say in how the site looks. Section 8(h) requires the Board to consult and actively involve local communities and stakeholders to ensure their ownership and cultural relevance.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Memorial Marker Act of 2024”.

Section 2 — Policy: promote unity, peace, justice and goodwill among all people; ensure the provision of basic necessities and equal opportunities and the promotion of social justice; ensure that indigenous peoples have the freedom to retain their distinct indigenous and ethnic identity in addition to their Bangsamoro political identity; and support the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, and enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology.

Section 3 — Defines shuhada as individuals who gave and devoted their lives, directly or indirectly, engaging in the armed struggle to assert the right to self-determination and freedom of the Bangsamoro.
Section 4 — The Bangsamoro Memorial Marker shall include a list of names of the shuhada.

Section 5 — Creates a Bangsamoro Eco-Park at Camp Abubakar, Municipality of Barira, Maguindanao del Norte, to be constructed, properly landscaped and designed with structures and ornaments reflective of Bangsamoro culture and arts, with complete facilities including a multi-purpose hall, children's playground, parking area, comfort rooms and wash areas, and access roads. The memorial marker is built within the eco-park.

Sections 6–7 — The marker and eco-park are constructed, maintained and managed under the supervision and control of a Bangsamoro Memorial Management Board, chaired by the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage with members from the Ministry of Public Works; the Ministry of Trade, Investments and Tourism; the Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta'; the Ministry of Basic, Higher, and Technical Education; the Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy; the local government unit of Barira; and a representative from each province of the region. The Commission also serves as secretariat.

Section 8 — Board functions: establish eligibility criteria for identifying and including names on the marker; determine the metes and bounds of the land area; engage in collaborations, partnerships and joint ventures with agencies, NGOs, academic institutions and businesses; ensure the establishment and functionality of a grievance mechanism; submit the final list of names to the Office of the Chief Minister; monitor construction against the set standards and designs; formulate plans, programmes, policies and rules; and consult and actively involve local communities and stakeholders in planning and development, ensuring their ownership and cultural relevance.

Section 9 — The Board dissolves on the completion and turnover of the marker and eco-park to the cultural heritage commission, with remaining assets, liabilities and ongoing matters transferred to it.
Section 10 — Necessary funds are provided in the annual appropriations of the Commission, with an initial ₱15,000,000 appropriated.

Section 11 — The Board may accept grants, donations and contributions in cash or in kind from public and private entities, domestic and foreign, and engage in collaborations and joint ventures, ensuring transparency and accountability and complying with all relevant reporting and regulatory requirements.
Section 14 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM.

citizen_questions.a: Section 3 defines them as individuals who gave and devoted their lives, directly or indirectly, engaging in the armed struggle to assert the right to self-determination and freedom of the Bangsamoro. 'Directly or indirectly' is deliberately wide.

citizen_questions.q: How is it decided whose name goes on the marker?
citizen_questions.a: The Bangsamoro Memorial Management Board establishes the eligibility criteria and submits the final list to the Office of the Chief Minister. The criteria are not written into the act.

citizen_questions.q: What if I disagree with a decision?
citizen_questions.a: Section 8(d) requires the Board to ensure the establishment and functionality of a grievance mechanism for the act's implementation.

No. The marker sits within an eco-park with a multi-purpose hall, children's playground, parking, comfort rooms and wash areas and access roads, landscaped and designed to reflect Bangsamoro culture and arts.

citizen_questions.q: How much does it cost, and can it take donations?
citizen_questions.a: ₱15 million initially, with further funds through the cultural heritage commission's annual budget. The Board may accept grants and donations, domestic and foreign, subject to transparency and reporting requirements.

citizen_questions.q: Who decides how big the park is?
citizen_questions.a: The Board determines the metes and bounds of the land area; the act does not fix them.
